title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom on 1968-03-16
lineage: SBD > MR > C > DAT > CDR > EAC (secure) > Cool Edit (minor fixes) > CD Wave (retracking) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: A classic March‑16‑68 soundboard capture with a smoking Alligator and strong Eleven, marred only by occasional tape cuts and modest hiss.
ai_review.review: The show is widely praised as one of the high points of ’68 – Garcia’s incendiary Alligator jam, the soaring Eleven, and the eerie Caution > Feedback sequence are highlighted repeatedly.  The soundboard source is generally clear for its era, though listeners note frequent drop‑outs, a bass‑heavy mix, and some muddy/hissy sections that keep it from being pristine.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (15+) give 4–5 stars and extol the musical performance; recording flaws are noted but do not dominate, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear for a 1968 tape, but suffers from frequent cuts/drop‑outs (especially around Cryptical and the start of Alligator), occasional heavy bass/muddy mids, and a hissy background.  Despite these issues the mix is listenable and captures the era’s ambience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical spring ’68 set – a psychedelic opener leading into extended jams, with the band weaving in and out of themes.  The second set builds momentum despite the tape cuts, delivering an especially powerful Alligator and a memorable Morning Dew.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work is lauded—especially the “mountain jam” licks in Alligator and his fire toward the end of the Eleven; a minor stumble noted at the start of China Cat.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as heavy/muddy but also praised for fine work on the Eleven and dancing with Jerry during Morning Dew.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s vocals are mentioned on the (unrecorded) “Dancin’ in the Street” encore; otherwise no specific remarks.
